transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2027-07-19
- Time: 16:00 PT
- Duration: ~58 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan, Priya, Liam, Anita (Redwood) — Marcus, Sofia, Priya B., Daniel (Velaris)

Auto-generated summary (may be incomplete): POC scoping for Velaris invoice automation and chat assist pilot. Focus on OpenAI-compatible endpoints + function calling to return structured JSON for invoices and support actions.

[00:00] Jordan Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out the time. Quick roll call?
[00:04] Marcus Lee: Marcus here, Sofia, Priya B. and Daniel on the line.
[00:08] Jordan Kim: Great. Objective for today is to align on success criteria and the bench plan for the six-week sprint. I'll pass to Priya to run through the technical mapping then we'll workshop the workload.
[00:20] Priya Rao: Cool. So from Redwood side we generally propose an OpenAI-compatible endpoint you can call with the same API surface. That maps to our hosted models, and we can wire up function calling — basically structured output as JSON schema. Important note: we'll present three model variants for the POC: a low-cost quantized 4-bit, a standard float32 open model, and a latency-optimized trimmed model.
[00:40] Sofia Alvarez: When you say "function calling" do you mean the same shaped payloads as the OpenAI function calling? So our backend can just ingest the returned JSON?
[00:46] Priya Rao: Yes, same semantics. We'll return a JSON object following the schema you provide. There's some nuance around streaming tokens vs final JSON — we recommend receiving the final object for heavy ETL workflows to avoid partial parse issues.
[00:59] Liam Torres: Also note we have structured-output validators in the SDK so errors are surfaced early. It will produce a content-check step and score structural validity.
[01:10] Marcus Lee: For success metrics — our PM wants p95 latency under 200ms for short chat calls, and for invoice extraction a correctness F1 of at least 92% on key fields. Are those realistic?
[01:19] Priya Rao: p95 200ms is tight but possible on Dedicated with the latency-optimized variant for short contexts (<256 tokens). For Hosted we'll probably see p95 around 250–400ms depending on concurrency. Will need to benchmark.
[01:31] Sofia Alvarez: Throughput-wise, we expect bursts to 150 RPS and sustained 40 RPS during business hours. That maps to about ~5M tokens/day estimated.
[01:43] Priya Rao: Okay, that token rate is helpful. We'll size the POC to simulate sustained 50 RPS and burst 200 RPS for the bench runs. We'll also do prefix/KV cache validation for repeated conversations to lower per-token cost.
[01:56] Daniel Cho: On infra: we need VPC peering, SAML SSO, and KMS for key management. Also: can you store KV cache in our infra or is it Redwood-managed?
[02:07] Liam Torres: KV cache is by default managed in-process on the server. For Private deployments we can configure a customer-managed cache backing but that adds ops to the scope. For the POC we recommend Redwood-hosted caching with logs, and we'll surface TTL and cache hits in the dashboard.
[02:22] Priya Banerjee: Our product team also wants structured telemetry so we can track per-field extraction accuracy over time. Can you attach evals to the pipeline?
[02:30] Priya Rao: Yes — Redwood Optimize supports eval hooks and quality regression alerts tied to prompt sets. For the POC we'll run nightly evals on a held-out set and feed results into the shared benchmark sheet.
[02:44] Jordan Kim: I just want to call out the success criteria we should lock:
- Latency: p95 <= 200ms for short chat (target), p95 <= 350ms acceptable
- Accuracy: invoice extraction F1 >= 92%
- Throughput: sustain 40 RPS, handle 200 RPS bursts without >10% error rate
- Cost guidance: target unit cost below $X per 1K tokens (we'll provide estimates)

[03:05] Marcus Lee: That aligns with our internal guardrails. We also need audit logs and data retention options — minimum 90 days of access logs.
[03:14] Anita Shah: We can produce audit logs and integrate with your SIEM; retention windows are configurable for Hosted trials. For private/on-prem we'd align with your compliance regime.
[03:24] Sofia Alvarez: Benchmarks — what are you going to run?
[03:27] Priya Rao: Two suites: 1) Chat/assist latency and quality with 5K synthetic prompts mirroring your traffic mix; 2) Invoice extraction -- 1.2K real-world docs you provide plus synthetic edge cases. We'll measure latency, tokens consumed, validator pass-rate, and extraction F1. We'll run across the three model variants and on two deployment targets (Redwood Hosted and Redwood Dedicated simulating your reserved pool).
[03:55] Priya Banerjee: For the invoice schema we'll need nested fields (line items, taxes). Can the SDK's structured validator handle nested arrays?
[04:03] Liam Torres: Yes, nested arrays are supported. We recommend providing JSON Schema or OpenAPI schema for the expected output; we'll embed that into the function schema for parser enforcement.
[04:16] Sofia Alvarez: Any changes we should be aware of around tokenization or min context length when comparing quantized vs float models?
[04:22] Priya Rao: Small differences exist. We'll normalize by tokenizing with the same tokenizer in the harness. Quantized models can slightly change output probabilities, so we'll track quality deltas per field.
[04:33] Marcus Lee: Timeline? You said six-week sprint earlier. Outline milestones please.
[04:36] Jordan Kim: Proposed schedule:
- Week 0 (this week): Align on success criteria, sample data, security requirements
- Week 1: Redwood sets up baseline harness and runs initial dry-run (hosted)
- Weeks 2–3: Full bench runs across variants, function-calling tests, structured validation
- Week 4: Integration tests with your ingestion pipeline + SSO/VPC checks (if needed)
- Week 5: Accuracy tuning and reruns, cost modeling
- Week 6: Wrap-up demo, runbook handoff and decision checkpoint

[05:12] Priya Banerjee: Sounds good. On the integration mapping: we'll want a small SDK shim that mirrors our existing OpenAI wrapper. How much effort to port?
[05:21] Priya Rao: Minimal. The Redwood SDK exposes OpenAI-style endpoints and a drop-in shim we can provide. For code-level differences, expect 1–2 developer-days to switch the base client. Function calling semantics are identical.
[05:34] Marcus Lee: Any obstacles for us around data privacy? We process PII in invoices.
[05:39] Anita Shah: For the POC we can enable data isolation and optional request-level encryption. We support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments. Also Redwood's hosted environment supports SOC2 controls and audit logs — we'll share the security pack after this call.
[05:53] Daniel Cho: We might want to run an initial benchmark on-prem to validate network egress. Is that in scope?
[05:58] Jordan Kim: We can do a simulated on-prem run via VPC peering for the POC, but a full on-prem install would be a separate engagement. We'll include the simulated run as part of Weeks 2–3.
[06:12] Sofia Alvarez: For measurement: can you surface per-request cost breakdowns in the console? Our finance team needs that.
[06:18] Liam Torres: Yes — token-level cost and per-route breakdowns are available. We'll export the cost curves per experiment into the benchmark sheet.
[06:26] Marcus Lee: Great. Any known limitations we should record?
[06:29] Priya Rao: Known items: streaming partial JSON can be tricky — we recommend single-call final JSON for invoice ETL; quantized variant may need a small prompt tuning step for parity on extraction tasks; some deep nested tables can be error-prone and require post-parse cleanup.
[06:47] Jordan Kim: Okay let's recap next steps — (1) Jordan sends POC playbook and benchmark harness link; (2) Velaris provides data and schema; (3) Redwood runs baseline hosted tests; (4) Infra sync between Priya and Daniel. We'll meet again in one week for check-in.
[06:59] Marcus Lee: Perfect — thanks everyone.
[07:01] Jordan Kim: Thanks, bye.

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings — e.g., "Redwood Dedicated" appeared as "Redwood Dedictated" in parts of the auto transcript. Links referenced during call: https://redwood.ai/poc/playbook (proto), https://docs.redwood.ai/benchmarks (prototype), shared benchmark sheet: https://sheets.google.com/velaris-redwood-poc (ACL restricted).
questions: Will the SDK shim fully replace OpenAI keys or is dual run supported?
How will nested invoice line-items be validated and what error tolerance is acceptable?
Do we have a contingency if Hosted latency doesn't meet p95 targets?
notes_for_csm: Velaris is risk-averse on PII; prioritize security pack and KMS options. Finance wants per-route cost estimates; attach cost curve. Schedule infra deep-dive with Daniel; expect some network constraints. Recommended: start with Hosted baseline then run Dedicated sim to validate latency targets.
